value.name: writes reminder in notebook
value.description: She replaces an old note with a new reminder about why she does the work.
evidence: She wrote in its place, in the same small handwriting, "remember why you do this work."

value.name: calls Marcus
value.description: Asha phones Marcus after making the note.

value.name: files codicil before office closes
value.description: Marcus files the codicil at the Register of Wills shortly before closing time.
evidence: Marcus had filed the codicil on Thursday evening at four-fifteen, twenty minutes before the Register of Wills closed.

value.name: drafts explanatory letter in car
value.description: Asha drafts the explanatory letter that accompanies the filing while riding back from the house.
evidence: he had filed it under cover of an explanatory letter that Asha had drafted in the car on the way back from the house
value.time_hint: on the way back from the house

value.name: pays filing fee from retainer
value.description: Marcus uses the retainer to pay the filing fee for the codicil.
evidence: he had paid the filing fee out of the retainer

value.name: secures stamped copy and scan
value.description: Marcus returns with both a stamped paper copy and a digital scan of the filed codicil.
evidence: he had brought back a stamped copy which was now in the file on her desk and a digital scan which was now in the cloud folder she shared with herself

value.name: reflects on document permanence
value.description: The narration frames the codicil as existing in multiple places, emphasizing its practical permanence.
evidence: The codicil existed, in other words, in the world in three places at once, which was as close to permanence as any document achieved in this profession.

value.name: warns that codicil will be contested
value.description: Marcus tells Asha that multiple parties may challenge the codicil.
evidence: "They will contest it," Marcus said, by way of greeting, when he picked up.

"Whoever is going to. The buyers, if they come back and find out the contingency they were depending on is gone. The brother, eventually, if he reverts to type. The IRS, conceivably, if the valuation comes in higher than the basis we are going to claim."

value.name: denies brother will contest
value.description: Asha insists that the brother will not challenge the codicil.
evidence: "The brother is not going to contest it."

value.name: admits uncertainty and hopes
value.description: Asha concedes she is not certain but is choosing hope despite her lack of coffee.
evidence: "I am not certain. I am hopeful. There is a difference and I am holding onto it because it is Friday morning and I have not had enough coffee."

value.name: Marcus reminds Asha she is not their friend
value.description: Marcus cautions Asha that she is not personally aligned with the people involved.

value.name: acknowledges professional distance
value.description: Asha briefly reacts to Marcus's warning and acknowledges it.
evidence: She held the phone away from her ear for a moment and then brought it back.
